title: BETWEEN TWO ARMIES
accuracyNotes: Arjuna's physical reaction (hand trembling, breath catching) is grounded in Gita 1.28-30, where his body falters and Gandiva slips from his hand.
Krishna's role as charioteer and guide is confirmed in Gita 1.21 and 2.47, with no endorsement of inaction or abandonment of duty.
The scene occurs at dawn at Kurukshetra, as described in scripture, with white horses, chariots, and banners present, though lighting and costumes are artistic interpretations.
The emotional core—duty, compassion, consequence—is derived from the Gita's exploration of inner conflict and moral responsibility, not external prophecy or divine intervention.

shots.action: Camera tracks slowly sideways past a stationary chariot wheel. A thin band of dust drifts across the ground. The white horse breathes. Preserve wheel geometry and distant figures in one uninterrupted shot.
shots.sound: gentle breeze, soft ambient dawn wind

shots.action: Close portrait: Arjuna's breath catches. Eyes shift toward distant army, then lower. Two loose hair strands move. Camera makes subtle push-in.
Hand-and-bow insert: hand trembles almost imperceptibly. Bow lowers slightly. Fingers remain on grip. Cloth shifts once. Camera holds still with natural drift.
Three-quarter portrait: Krishna turns gently, makes one small calm nod, breathes naturally. Yellow cloth and feather move in breeze. Subtle camera push.
Over-shoulder: Arjuna steadies breathing, lifts eyes to Krishna. Only one face visible. Camera moves slightly laterally to reveal chariot rail. Both bodies stable. Flags move gently.
Profile close: Arjuna raises gaze slightly. Jaw relaxes. Takes one steady breath. Camera glides forward slightly. Hair and flags move in soft wind. Face and wardrobe unchanged.
